newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig reports 631 mln DM 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Grundig reports 631 mln DM 1996 loss.

text.p: Embattled German audio-visual equipment manufacturer Grundig AG said on Monday it lost a record 631 million marks ($368.4 million) in 1996, compared with a 598 million mark loss the year before.
In March, the company estimated the 1996 loss at 553 million marks.
A Grundig spokesman said the loss was larger due to 70 million marks ($40.9 million) in additional restructuring costs.
The company's account for 1996, approved on Monday by the supervisory board, showed sales of 3.3 billion marks, down five percent from the previos year.
The 1996 loss will be covered by Grundig's former parent company Philips, which withdrew its support at the start of this year.
The spokesman said the company's goal was to reduce its loss to below 100 million marks this year, on sales of about three billion marks, and to break even next year.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.713 German Marks)
